items.definition:
a small settlement, generally one smaller than a village
They lived in a quiet hamlet nestled in the valley.

sadness because one has no friends or company
She felt a deep sense of loneliness after moving to a new city.

an intermittent and remittent fever caused by a protozoan parasite that invades the red blood cells
Travelers to tropical regions should take precautions against malaria.

a follower of Methodism, a Protestant Christian denomination
She grew up in a Methodist family.

a building or buildings occupied by a community of monks living under religious vows
The monks lived a quiet life in the ancient monastery.

a change in the genetic structure of an organism or a significant change
The mutation caused a significant change in the plant's appearance.

failure to take proper care in doing something
The accident was caused by the driver's negligence.

the quality in a sound of being deep, full, and reverberating or the quality of evoking a response
The speech had a strong emotional resonance with the audience.

the rescue of a wrecked or disabled ship or its cargo
They attempted to salvage what was left after the fire.

the use of humor, irony, exaggeration, or ridicule to expose and criticize people's stupidity or vices
The play was a sharp satire on modern politics.

a point of view or position from which something is considered or assessed
From my standpoint, the decision was unfair.

a large earthenware or stoneware drinking mug, typically for beer
He drank beer from a traditional stein.

a constitutional right to reject a decision or proposal made by a law-making body
The President exercised his veto power.

in cricket, one of the two sets of three stumps with two bails on top
The bowler took a crucial wicket.

a metallic element
Zinc is often used to coat steel to prevent rust.

a stick used by a conductor or police officer
The conductor raised his baton to begin the symphony.

a plant whose leaves are used to make cocaine
The coca plant is native to South America.

a small sheltered bay
We anchored our boat in a quiet cove.

a lack or shortage
Iron deficiency can cause fatigue.

a country governed by a dictator
The country was ruled by a harsh dictatorship for decades.

great fear or apprehension
She felt a sense of dread as the deadline approached.

a model of a human, or a foolish person
The crash test dummy was used to simulate impact.

the process of eroding or being eroded by wind, water, or other natural agents
Soil erosion is a major environmental problem.

exhibition; exposition
We visited the new art expo downtown.

side (of an animal or building)
The general ordered his troops to attack the enemy's flank.

a sudden burst of light or fire
The ship sent up a distress flare.

the occurrence, rate, or frequency of a disease, crime, or other undesirable thing
The incidence of flu increases in winter.

close familiarity or friendship
They shared a moment of quiet intimacy.

Local Area Network
We set up a LAN party to play games together.

the number of miles traveled or covered
This car gets good mileage on the highway.

an organism that has undergone mutation
The scientists studied the new mutant strain of bacteria.

a collection of myths, especially one belonging to a particular religious or cultural tradition
Greek mythology is full of fascinating stories.

an annoying person or thing; a destructive insect
Mosquitoes are a real pest in the summer.

a tall vertical structure
The ancient temple was supported by stone pillars.

rain, snow, sleet, or hail
We expect some precipitation later today.

a period of isolation
The travelers had to go into quarantine for two weeks.

a question or inquiry
The customer had a query about their order.

control over one's emotions or actions
He showed great restraint despite the provocation.

an underground pipe for waste water
The city's sewers are being repaired.

a person who speaks on behalf of a group
The company's spokesperson issued a statement.

a Muslim sovereign
The sultan ruled over a vast empire.

a particular attitude or way of considering a matter
From my viewpoint, the plan is flawed.

official connection to a group
Her political affiliation is with the Green Party.

a confident and forceful statement of fact or belief
His assertion that he was innocent was not believed.

an account of a person's life written by that person
She wrote an autobiography about her childhood.

a religion and philosophy originating in India
Buddhism emphasizes peace and mindfulness.

a hidden store of things; a computer memory
The browser stores a cache of frequently visited pages.

the process of trying to acquire or develop a quality or skill
The cultivation of new ideas is essential for progress.

lack of respect or courtesy
Showing disrespect to elders is considered rude.

an improvement or addition to something
The software update includes several performance enhancements.

an official order or decree
The government issued a fiat to control prices.

a joke or trick; something put in or over a person's mouth to prevent them from speaking
The comedian told a funny gag.

the respiratory organ of fish and some amphibians
Fish use their gills to breathe underwater.

a dish of cooked meat and potatoes; a symbol (#)
She ordered corned beef hash for breakfast.

hydroelectric power; water
The region relies heavily on hydro for its electricity.

an aromatic evergreen shrub; a symbol of honor or victory
The athlete rested on his laurels after winning the championship.

a person with left-wing political views
Many leftists advocate for social equality.

a raised platform for a speaker or conductor
The speaker stood on the podium to address the crowd.

a religious or other solemn ceremony or act
The wedding was a beautiful rite of passage.

a smaller part of a larger whole; a housing development
The new subdivision has many houses.

a tax or duty to be paid on a particular class of imports or exports
The government imposed a new tariff on imported goods.

a device or person that tracks something
The fitness tracker monitors my steps.

a machine for producing continuous power in which a wheel or rotor is made to revolve by a fast-moving flow of water, steam, gas, or air
Wind turbines generate electricity.

ultraviolet (radiation)
Wear sunscreen to protect against UV rays.
